title: A Baby Turkey, a Feather Duster Mom, and a Best Friend
summary:
It sounds like something straight out of a Disney movie: two wild animals from different species becoming best friends. That is exactly what happened at the Raven Ridge Wildlife Center in southeastern Pennsylvania, between a baby turkey and a mourning dove.

Last spring, the wildlife center took in two orphaned turkey chicks, called poults. To calm them down, the team placed them with a feather duster as a stand-in mother turkey. Turkey poults stress easily and are hard to rehabilitate. Sadly, one of them did not survive.

The center never raises baby animals alone, so the team needed a companion for the remaining chick. They paired it with a baby mourning dove of a similar size, hoping the two would comfort each other while eating and exploring, since both feed on the ground.

The pairing worked better than anyone expected. The two formed a bond the center had never seen before. Months later, the team gave the dove a soft release, meaning it could leave whenever it wanted. But the dove clearly had no plans to go. It kept returning to the turkey's cage, and the two would sit near each other on either side of the fence. After a few days, the team put the dove back in with the turkey, and it was clear they were happiest together.

Keeping them caged for life just because they were cute was not an option, the center said, and would not be fair to wild animals. So the team contacted a large sanctuary in Pennsylvania to arrange a joint release, letting the pair choose whether to stay together or go their own ways. After the soft release, the dove flew into the trees and the turkey started foraging, free to stick together or join others of their own kind. The center does not know if they will stay together, but made sure they had a safe place until they were ready to be on their own.
why_it_matters: The story shows how wildlife centers try to care for orphaned animals in a way that respects their wild nature, and how friendship can form in unexpected places.
